newsitem.title: BRAZIL: South American port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: South American port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

BRAZIL, Sept 24 - Vitoria - eight vessels berthed of which 1 container/general cargo discharger/loader, 1 general cargo loader/discharger, 2 granite loaders, 1 cellulose loader, 2 wheat dischargers, 1 pig iron loader. Tubarao 3 iron ore loaders. Praia Mole 3 steel plate loaders, 2 bulk coal dischargers. Portocel 1 cellulose loader. Ubu 1 iron ore loader. 22 vessels waiting in roads. Santos - 39 berthed of which 6 full containers, 3 general, 1 bulk cement discharger, 15 sugar loaders, 2 chemical products dischargers, 3 wheat dischargers, 3 fertiliser dischargers, 1 coal loader, 1 salt discharger, 1 fruit loader, 1 paper loader, 1 steel products loader, 1 reefer loader. 30 vessels waiting in roads, 90 due over next 7 days. Private terminals Cosipa 2 steel products loaders, 1 iron ore discharger. Rio Grande - 10 berthed of which 3 bulk fertiliser dischargers, 2 full containers, 2 soy loaders, 1 wheat discharger, 1 soybean loader, 1 wood. 4 waiting in roads, 29 due over the next 10 days. Sao Sebastiao - Tebar 2 vessels berthed. Commercial quay 1 berthed, 1 waiting in roads, 9 due over the next 7 days. Rio de Janeiro - ten berthed of which 1 container discharger, 2 general cargo/ steel products dischargers, 2 wheat dischargers, 2 general cargo dischargers, 2 sugar loaders, 1 steel products loader. Tecon 1 berthed, 44 due over next 7 days. Itajai - three vessels berthed of which 1 general cargo, 2 reefers. 6 waiting in roads, 14 due in next 7 days.

VENEZUELA, Sept 23 - Puerto Cabello - ten vessels berthed of which 3 grain, 6 general cargo, 1 containers. 1 vessel anchored, piers 1 and 2 closed. Guanta - two general cargo vessels berthed, No vessels anchored. Conditions Sept 24 - all ports working normally. Orinoco River - draft today 37 ft 6 ins. Puerto Ordaz - two vessels operating of which 1 discharging manganese ore, 1 loading iron ore. 5 vessels due. Palua - one vessel loading iron ore. Boca Grande - one vessel loading iron ore, 2 vessels due. Mile 178 - three vessels waiting at anchorage to load/discharge. Matanzas - two vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 5 vessels operating of which 2 loading steel products, 1 loading/discharging general cargo, 3 discharging (1 bentonite, 1 scrap, 1 coke), 5 vessels due. Venalum - two vessels loading aluminium. Alcasa - one vessel discharging wire rods. San Felix - one vessel loading aluminium. Punta Cuchillo - one vessel due. Puerto Cabello - one vessel waiting at anchorage to load/discharge. 11 vessels operating of which 8 loading/discharging general cargo, 2 discharging grain, 1 discharging steel products, 10 vessels due. Bajo Grande - one vessel loading refined products. Buoy B.71 - one vessel due. Guanta - two vessels operating, both discharging, of which 1 tuna, 1 pipes. 6 vessels due. Amuay - six vessels loading refined products. Guaranao - two vessels discharging wood pulp. La Guaira - two vessels due, 3 vessels under repairs.
